checks.detail: Every forge output is byte-identical to the compared output of the same build on stanley (outputs-sha256.txt).
checks.name: outputs

manifest.binary: The sparkles CLI built with mbx build --release -p sparkles-server on stanley at commit 71fcf893 and copied to the benchmark host
manifest.lock_note: The lock passed from the post-push benchmark check, so the first round includes that run's tail and is the slowest in every row. The tables use medians.

reference.robot: robot reason with ELK from runs/2026-11-03-reasoners-forge-ea96e8f5 on the same host and files, median of three, 14.04 s at 3,597 MiB on GO and 30.63 s at 8,287 MiB on ChEBI lite. ROBOT's reduce, relax and chain have no figures from this host.

method: forge-sparkles.sh.txt took ~/lanes/.bench.lock once and ran three interleaved rounds. Each round timed, on GO and ChEBI lite from the release's RDF/XML file, sparkles ontology reason, reduce and relax with --input and --output to a functional-style file, the chain reason --input FILE relax reduce --output FILE, and sparkles ontology classify FILE --format ofn --allow-unsatisfiable, each through timed.py.txt, which records the wall time, the peak resident set and the exit status in runs.jsonl. robot-compare.txt is scripts/elk-compare/ofn-axioms.py --all between lane 604's ROBOT 1.9.11 outputs with ELK 0.6.0 and the same build's outputs on stanley, and outputs-sha256.txt shows the forge outputs are byte-identical to those.
scale: GO 2026-07-26 and ChEBI lite 256, RDF/XML releases
